Hello, Reddit! I'm coming to you from Fredericton, NB after the storm. It's been over 30 hours for us since the electricity went off, and crews are working around the clock. I'm actually at a friend's place typing this so you know what's been going on in the city. Starting from around 11 yesterday, over 36,000 people lost power in the city alone, and by the end of the day 53,000 in the extended Fredericton area. The storm was more than any of us expected, with trees and power lines snapping and falling down. In fact, on Waterloo Row an old tree was completely uprooted (I estimate it was probably around 50 feet tall, and really thick). With the majority of the city without power, people found they couldn't cook hot meals, so lineups started forming at the restaurants that were left. It got to the point that the Greco on Dundonald ran out of dough for pizzas after trucking in the entirety of it from Oromocto. There are only 2 Tim Horton's that are operational in the city to my knowledge, and only 2 McDonald's, so this morning the lines for Breakfast went out of the parking lot and out of the door. If I didn't have to conserve power for my phone, I would've taken pictures. A church in the Downtown core is actually holding a Pot Luck dinner for members where they can bring any and all food that might go bad in their fridges, since from what we've heard a lot of us might not get power until Tuesday. It's been a real change for this city, and not nearly as bad as other places, but for us this was quite a ride. At any rate, we're all alive and well! Just trees all over the place and no AC. TL;DR - First World Problems EDIT - On the North Side, we discovered that somehow someone's sunflowers survived the storm. This person had divine intervention.

The New York Yankees acquire Brandon McCarthy from the Arizona Diamondbacks. Taking a quick look at McCarthy's stats this season doesn't look too promising for the Yankees. He's put up a 5.01 ERA through 109.2 innings, with a 7.6 K/9 rate and a 1.6 K/9. Digging a little deeper, however, tells a different story. His FIP sits at a respectable 3.79, his xFIP even better at 2.89. Advanced statistics seem to favor a better future for McCarthy. So what's driving that ERA up? Likely a combination of an unusually high BABIP (batters are putting up a .345 BABIP against him) and an even more unusual 20% HR/FB ratio. His pitches are leaping off the bats of his opponents at what's likely an unsustainable rate. He's a much better pitcher than the surface stats tell.

That being said, I'm not sure McCarthy's BABIP will regress back to his career average of .298. Going to the New York Yankees, who's middle infield defense is questionable at best. Fangraphs peg Brian Roberts Defense rating at a -3.0, while Derek Jeter gets a 0.8. Having Brett Gardner and Jacoby Ellsbury in the outfield will help, but I expect a regression to last year's BABIP of .325 to be more reasonable. This still gives the Yankees another servicable starter, something they need as they wait on the news for CC Sabathia.

The Arizona Diamondbacks get Vidal Nuno, a 26 year old lefty starting pitcher. Nuno comes with plenty of team control, but his stats tell a different story than McCarthy's. Through 78.0 innings pitched, Nuno's produced a 5.42 ERA with a 6.9 K/9 vs a 3.0 BB/9. While it looked like McCarthy had been unlucky, Nuno's just been plain bad. His 5.15 FIP and 4.41 xFIP don't exactly inspire the thought of improvement. And unlike McCarthy, there's no high BABIP (.301) or ridiculously high HR/FB ratio (14%) to bail him out. A move to the National League may help, but don't expect too much.

Nuno probably slots in as McCarthy's replacement in Arizona's rotation. Players don't hit badly against him at any number of times facing him, so the odds of him being a better reliever than starter are pretty low.

Advantage: New York Yankees. I've gotta give this one to the Yanks. They got a starter who's going to get better than he's been so far for a cheap price. Getting Arizona to eat some of the salary remaining on his contract was just the icing on the cake for New York.
